# MongoDB 8.0 performance changes & known regressions vs 7.0

<!-- provenance: generated by /dr deep-research 2026-07-14 · topic: "MongoDB 8.0 performance changes and known read-path regressions vs 7.0" · sources: 28 (docs/jira/blog/forum) · verified-as-of: 2026-07-14 -->

What actually changed in the 8.0 engine that affects latency/throughput, what the official benchmark claims do and don't say, and every known post-GA regression report — with per-claim confidence. Confidence tiers: **FACT** = 3+ independent sources; **QUALIFIED** = 2; **TENTATIVE** = single-source or contested.

## Express execution path (point reads)

- 8.0 adds EXPRESS plan stages — `EXPRESS_IXSCAN`, `EXPRESS_CLUSTERED_IXSCAN`, `EXPRESS_UPDATE`, `EXPRESS_DELETE` — for a limited query set that bypasses regular query planning for optimized index-scan plans (new in 8.0). **FACT** [^1][^3][^27]
- Origin: an 8.0 "tiger team" experiment hard-coded reads past the planner; it improved YCSB 100%-read significantly and was productized as ExpressPlan, extended to updates/deletes and unique-index lookups (`_id`/unique-index point ops). **QUALIFIED** [^3]
- Third-party write-ups cite ~17% latency gain for express-eligible (IDHACK-style `_id` lookup) workloads; the figure is not in official docs. **TENTATIVE** [^27]
- Express plans skip the multi-planner and surface as EXPRESS stages in explain/slow-query logs; plan-cache/index-filter tuning does not apply to them (plan-cache bypass implied, not stated verbatim in docs). **TENTATIVE on the plan-cache detail** [^4]
- Regression on this path: SERVER-97911 — `_id: {$in: []}` (empty array) + `_id` index hint fell off the fast path and full-scanned the collection; affects 8.0.1+, fixed 8.0.6. **QUALIFIED** [^14]

## Query engine: SBE vs classic

The single most upgrade-relevant engine fact — **which execution engine runs changed underneath 7.0 users mid-patch-series**:

- SBE was NOT removed in 8.0; classic remains for ineligible queries, SBE handles a restricted set (most commonly `$group`/`$lookup` pushdown). **FACT** [^5]
- **7.0.17+ default-disabled SBE**: "Starting in version 7.0.17, the slot-based query execution engine is no longer enabled by default for patch versions of 7.0… please upgrade to version 8.0, where it is enabled by default." (SERVER-94735 set `internalQueryFrameworkControl` to `forceClassicEngine` on 7.0.) **FACT** [^5][^6]
- Engine-control lineage: 6.x `trySbeEngine` (broad) → 7.0/7.2 `trySbeRestricted` ($group/$lookup only, SERVER-83685) → 7.0.17+ `forceClassicEngine` → 8.0 `trySbeRestricted` again by default. **QUALIFIED** [^5][^6]
  - Practical implication: a workload tested on 7.0.17+ (e.g. 7.0.37) ran **classic engine**; the same workload on 8.0.x runs **restricted SBE** for eligible shapes. A 7.0.37 → 8.0.x comparison is also an engine-default comparison for `$group`/`$lookup` aggregations — not for plain finds, which stay classic/express in both.
- Rollback background: SBE plan-cache/multiplanning defects in 7.x, e.g. SERVER-84338 (top-level `$or` → invalid SBE plan-cache entry → wrong results; affects 7.0.4–7.2.0, fixed 7.0.6/7.2.1). **QUALIFIED** [^18]
- 8.0 SBE additions: time-series block processing (200%+ faster analytical `$group` vs 7.0); per-query-shape engine pinning via query settings. **QUALIFIED** [^1]

## Plan cache & query settings

- Index filters deprecated in 8.0; replaced by persistent cluster-wide query settings (`setQuerySettings`) + operation rejection filters. **FACT** [^7][^27]
- `queryHash` renamed `planCacheShapeHash` (old field kept, deprecated) — affects slow-query-log tooling. **QUALIFIED** [^7]
- Field-reported (not release-noted) default changes seen in a getParameter diff between 7.0.5 and 8.0.1: `internalQueryExecYieldIterations` 1000 → −1; `internalQueryCardinalityEstimatorMode` sampling → heuristic. **TENTATIVE** [^19]

## TCMalloc rewrite

- 8.0 replaces gperftools-era TCMalloc with upstream Google TCMalloc using **per-CPU caches** (was per-thread), reducing fragmentation under high-stress workloads; `serverStatus` gains `tcmalloc.usingPerCPUCaches`. **FACT** [^1][^8][^12]
- Per-CPU cache preconditions: Linux kernel ≥ 4.18; **THP enabled** (`always`, defrag `defer+madvise`, `max_ptes_none=0`) — a reversal of pre-8.0 best practice; glibc rseq disabled. Any unmet condition → silent fallback to legacy per-thread caches. **FACT** [^8][^12]
- `tcmallocEnableBackgroundThread` on by default (returns memory to OS periodically); `tcmallocReleaseRate` default 0 (deprecated). **QUALIFIED** [^2][^8]
- Percona dedicated test (PSMDB 8.0.16-5 vs 7.0.26-14, 4 vCPU/4 GB, POCDriver ×4 threads): 8.0 ahead — inserts +28.6%, `_id` lookups +34.3%, range +37.5%, updates +22.6%; ~18% lower fragmentation. **QUALIFIED** [^12]
- Small-instance (≤2 vCPU) downside: **no documented regression found** (explicit negative result). Structural note: the design target is allocator contention across many cores; benefit shrinks at low concurrency, and the silent fallback can negate the feature. **TENTATIVE** [^8][^12]

## batchedDeletes / TTL

- Batched deletes predate both versions (since 6.1; `BATCHED_DELETE` stage; TTL monitor single-threaded, targets 500 docs/1000 ms per sub-pass — SERVER-56194). **FACT** [^9][^28]
- No intentional batched-delete behavior change 7.0 → 8.0 (v7.0/v8.0 manual text identical). 8.0 changes nearby: `EXPRESS_DELETE` for point deletes; new server-level multi-collection `bulkWrite` ("up to 56% faster"). **QUALIFIED** [^9][^1]
- Fixes in the 8.0.x series: SERVER-97368 (TTL deletes silently skipped on time-series collections with pre-1970 timestamps; fixed 8.0.12) — note one blog (JusDB) misdescribes this as a 8.0.4 lock-timeout loop "fixed in 8.0.5"; JIRA contradicts that account. SERVER-95570 (BatchedDeleteStage can find the record it deletes twice; fixed 8.0.20/7.0.35/8.2.2). **QUALIFIED**; JusDB account **CONTESTED** [^15][^16][^25][^26]

## Replication & write-concern changes

- **Majority-ack semantics changed in 8.0**: `w:majority` writes ack when the majority have **written the oplog entry**, not (as before) applied the change. Documented caveat: a secondary read immediately after a majority-acked write (no causally-consistent session) may not see the write. **FACT** [^1][^2][^3]
- Secondaries write and apply oplog batches in parallel (separate writer/applier threads); `metrics.repl.buffer.*` split into `.write.*`/`.apply.*` (breaking metrics change). **FACT** [^1][^2]
- The "up to 20% faster concurrent writes during replication" claim originates in MongoDB's own release notes/product pages, mechanically backed by the two changes above; ack-after-journal was prototyped in a week, validated ~3 months incl. TLA+ modeling. **FACT (claim origin; the 20% itself is vendor-internal)** [^1][^3][^10]
- 8.0's stated program goal: claw performance back to the 4.4 era (5.0's `w:majority` default traded speed for durability); 8.0 added instruction-count CI benchmarks (0.2% tolerance, 5% revert rule) to block new regressions. **QUALIFIED** [^3]
- Compatibility caveat: shutdown after heavy bulk-ingest can take longer (extra data flushing). **QUALIFIED** [^2]

## Official benchmark claims

- Official 8.0-vs-7.0 numbers: 36% faster reads, 32% faster 95/5 mixed, 59% higher update throughput, 56% faster bulk writes, 24% faster Linkbench, 200%+ faster time-series aggregations, 20% faster concurrent writes during replication — "internal testing with public benchmarks" (YCSB, Linkbench, TSBS). **FACT** [^1][^10]
- **MongoDB does not publish the hardware/instance sizes** behind those numbers; the only hedges are "precise gains will vary from application to application" and "…can vary depending on the configuration of your workloads and database instances." No official small-tier caveat exists. **FACT (verified absence)** [^1][^3][^10]
- Independent replication on mid-size hardware (Percona, mongo-perf, n2-standard-8, 8.0.4 vs 7.0.15): +12%/1 thread, +7%/4 threads, +9%/8 threads, up to 20–30% on some tests, **no regressions observed**. **QUALIFIED** [^11]
- Published critique: the 36% headline is measured against 7.0 — itself a weakened baseline (7.0-era execution-control/ticket-throttling regression vs 6.0, mitigated by pinning `storageEngineConcurrentRead/WriteTransactions` to 128 and later 7.0.x fixes) — so gains vs 6.0 are smaller. **QUALIFIED** [^22][^23]
- FCV nuance: on 8.0 binaries, reads measured slightly faster with FCV 7 than FCV 8 (Percona FCV study). **TENTATIVE** [^13]

## Known regression reports

Post-GA "8.0 slower" catalog (as of 2026-07-14). Net assessment: **no widespread, confirmed 8.0 read-latency regression vs 7.0 exists in the public record**; confirmed items are edge-case and fixed by 8.0.6–8.0.20; broader reports are isolated, unresolved, or contested.

| # | Report | Affected | Fixed | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SERVER-97911 — `_id $in []` + `_id` hint → full collection scan | 8.0.1+ | 8.0.6 | jira [^14] |
| 2 | SERVER-101800 — OpenSSL 3.2.x HMAC regression, high CPU with TLS even under light load | ≤8.0.5 (w/ openssl-3.2.2-6.el9_5) | 8.0.12 / 7.0.23 | jira [^17] |
| 3 | SERVER-97368 — TTL deletes silently skipped, time-series w/ pre-1970 timestamps | ≤8.0.11 | 8.0.12 | jira [^15] |
| 4 | SERVER-95570 — BatchedDeleteStage double-enqueue | 7.x/8.x | 8.0.20 / 7.0.35 | jira [^16] |
| 5 | Forum — FETCH degradation 7.0.5→8.0.1: indexed `$match` agg 30s → ~1,100s; saveState/restoreState 3,187 → 45,999; user noted `internalQueryExecYieldIterations` 1000 → −1. No staff reply, no ticket | 8.0.1 | unresolved | forum, TENTATIVE [^19] |
| 6 | Forum — replica-set throughput drop on 8.0.1 (and 7.0.15/5.0.30) vs 4.4.29: transactional bulkWrite ~50% fewer ops/s, Java driver, w:0 | 8.0.1 | unresolved | forum, TENTATIVE [^20] |
| 7 | DBA SE — CPU regression 8.0.15–8.0.20: find with `$in` (28 `_id`s) + deep projections, planningTimeMicros ~1.96s; rollback to 8.0.14 restores. No ticket identified | 8.0.15–8.0.20 | unresolved/contested | forum, TENTATIVE [^21] |
| 8 | SERVER-125325 — view create/drop degrades with view count (catalog copying) | 8.0.x | open | jira, TENTATIVE |
| 9 | HN microbenchmark — 8.0.4 slower than 3.4.24 on rapid-increment loop; rebutted in-thread | 8.0.4 | contested | forum, TENTATIVE [^24] |
| 10 | Counter-evidence — Percona 8.0.4-vs-7.0.15 suite: no regressions; the famous 7.0-era read regression (WT ticket throttling) is pre-8.0 context, reported fixed by 8.0 | 7.0.x | in 8.0 | blog [^11][^23] |

## Diagnostic checklist

For a suspected 7.0 → 8.0 read-latency regression:

1. **Pin down the patch versions.** 7.0.17+ ran classic engine by default; 8.0 runs restricted SBE. For `$group`/`$lookup` aggregations, the upgrade silently changed engines — compare `explain` `queryFramework` fields ("classic" vs "sbe") across versions.
2. **Check express eligibility.** Point reads on `_id`/unique index should show EXPRESS stages in 8.0 explain — if they don't, ask why (hint? empty `$in` on ≤8.0.5? non-unique index?).
3. **Check the version against the regression catalog above** — especially 8.0.1–8.0.5 (SERVER-97911), ≤8.0.11 TLS/OpenSSL CPU (SERVER-101800), 8.0.15–8.0.20 `$in`+projection reports.
4. **Verify TCMalloc mode** — `serverStatus().tcmalloc.usingPerCPUCaches`; on managed platforms confirm THP posture. Silent fallback = you're not getting the 8.0 allocator at all.
5. **planningTimeMicros** in slow-query logs / profiler — the contested 8.0.15+ reports localize to planning, not execution.
6. **Compare `planCacheShapeHash`** (renamed from `queryHash`) when diffing slow-query logs across the upgrade — same shape, different field name.
7. **Sub-100ms operations never hit the slow-query log** (default `slowms` 100) — use the profiler (`db.setProfilingLevel(1, {slowms: N})`), Atlas Query Profiler, or `$queryStats` for millisecond-scale regressions.
